items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: Adolphus Allbrooks was on the bass... Lester was on tenor. I forgot the trumpet player's name, but it was his band.

ctx.x: He was very light complexion. And he just turned blue all around there because he bled inwardly, you know. And he died right away. They said he -- it was instant death with him. And anyway, we went on to Minneapolis and we did the show. I had a broken ankle. And we didn't -- they were short a tenor player. So, in Minneapolis there was a little band playing out at the Cotton Club. And the guy said, well, there's a good tenor player out there. Why don't you try to get him.

So, we went out there and listened to the guy. Earl -- we told Earl the guy was real good. And somebody told Earl the guy didn't read real good. So, he didn't get him. Instead he got Budd -- instead Budd Johnson. But the guy was Lester Young. That was Lester Young. And the little band he was playing out there with was a guy named Pugh played the drums, and Adolphus Allbrooks was on the bass. Lester was on tenor. I forgot the trumpet player's name, but it was his band. I can't think of his name right now, but they…
